title: Expose active profile pack version in /health and debug endpoints
author: Omar El-Sayed
release_notes: On-call triage: /health and authenticated debug endpoints now include profile_pack metadata (profile_pack_version, profile_id, sku/driver) to speed up perf regression investigation.
description:
Motivation
We’ve had multiple canary/rollout investigations where the first question is “what profile pack version is this pool actually running?” and the answer requires ssh’ing into a node or scraping runtime logs. This PR makes that information discoverable via /health and the existing debug endpoints so SRE can validate profile adoption quickly, correlate with perf-canary deltas, and shorten time-to-mitigation.

Scope
- Add profile pack metadata to /health response (safe, non-sensitive)
- Add richer profile details to authenticated debug endpoints
- Ensure we don’t leak customer override payloads (only the resolved/active values + provenance)
- Add unit tests and golden snapshots for schema stability

What changed
1) /health
- Adds a new optional object under runtime:
  - profile_pack_version (string)
  - active_profile_id (string)
  - hardware_sku (string, e.g., H100-SXM, L40S-PCIe)
  - cuda_version (string)
  - nvidia_driver (string)
  - selection_reason (string; high-level, e.g. “sku_match + cuda_compat”; no customer identifiers)

Example (trimmed):
GET /health
{
  "status": "ok",
  "runtime": {
    "version": "1.22.0",
    "profile_pack_version": "1.0.0",
    "active_profile_id": "h100/latency-balanced/v3",
    "hardware_sku": "H100-SXM",
    "cuda_version": "12.4",
    "nvidia_driver": "550.54.14",
    "selection_reason": "sku_match+cuda_compat"
  }
}

2) Debug endpoints
- /debug/runtime (existing): now includes the same fields as /health plus knob provenance:
  - knobs_source: "pack_default" | "fleet_override" | "customer_pin" | "local_override"
  - profile_pack_sha (git sha of the pack bundle embedded in the runtime build)
- /debug/config (existing): adds profile_pack section with resolved values only. Explicitly does NOT return raw override payloads.

Security / privacy
- /health remains unauthenticated in some environments (Hosted). We only include coarse metadata that is not tenant-specific.
- For debug endpoints, we preserve current auth checks. Additionally:
  - We do not return per-customer override identifiers or the unredacted override config.
  - selection_reason is intentionally high-level (no fleet pool name, no region, no customer).

Compatibility
- /health: fields are additive and optional; no existing keys removed.
- Added a schema_version bump for internal golden snapshots only (external clients should treat unknown fields as ignorable).

Testing
- Unit tests for HealthPayload serialization with/without profile pack loaded
- Golden snapshot updates for /debug/runtime response
- Added regression test to ensure redaction for override payloads

Operational notes
- This should reduce time-to-triage for incidents like elevated p99 tail latency after profile default changes.
- Intended to be consumed by on-call debug bundles (ref: INT-8831) and by perf-canary dashboards (label join on profile_pack_version).

Follow-ups (out of scope)
- Add profile_pack_version to Console runtime instance detail panel (tracked separately)
- Wire these fields into the standard support bundle export path (SRE runbook update)

Risk
Low. Additive response fields only; guarded by existing auth for detailed debug endpoints.
commits: runtime/health: include active profile pack metadata
debug endpoints: add profile_pack_version + redacted provenance
conversation:
Allison Grant (review): Can we ensure these fields are tagged consistently with what we’re emitting in metrics (profile_id vs active_profile_id)? Would prefer we standardize naming before this propagates.

Omar El-Sayed (author): Good call. I updated /health to use active_profile_id (explicit that it’s resolved) but debug endpoint also includes profile_id as an alias for consistency with metrics. Metrics remain profile_id. Added a comment + test to ensure both are in sync.

Sean Gallagher (review): /health is unauth in Hosted. Are we comfortable returning driver/CUDA? It’s probably fine but I want to avoid anything that can be used for targeted probing.

Omar El-Sayed (author): I can remove driver minor if you want. Current thinking: driver/CUDA is already inferable from perf characteristics and isn’t tenant-specific; also very useful for diagnosing compatibility gates. I kept it but limited it to the string versions only (no device UUIDs, no hostnames). If we want to be stricter, we can gate these fields behind the same auth as debug.

Noah Patel (review): Let’s keep driver/CUDA. We’ve had B200 bring-up issues due to mismatches; having this in /health is valuable. But please ensure selection_reason doesn’t accidentally include pool name/region.

Omar El-Sayed (author): Updated selection_reason to a fixed enum-ish string computed from rule matches (sku_match, cuda_compat, driver_compat, fallback_to_safe). Added unit test to prevent free-form logging from leaking through.

Julian Moore (review): Request: add to /debug/runtime a single-line summary that matches the startup log so on-call can copy/paste into the incident channel.

Omar El-Sayed (author): Added runtime_profile_summary field in /debug/runtime: "profile_pack=1.0.0 profile=h100/latency-balanced/v3 sku=H100-SXM cuda=12.4 driver=550.54.14 source=pack_default".

Sean Gallagher (approval): Approved with the redaction test. Please link this PR in the SRE checklist doc once merged.

Merge: Squashed and merged.
